correctness.rationale: For g,h in UT4(Fq) with six coordinates each, direct group multiplication yields u=aD-Ad, v=dF-Df, w=aE+bF-Ae-Bf-(f+F)u; c,C are free and contribute q^2. For fixed u,v the outer sextuples (a,d,f,A,D,F) number S=q^2(q^2-1)+q^4*1_{u=v=0}, since (d,D)!=0 gives q choices each for (a,A),(f,F), otherwise u=v=0 and four free. The linear w constraint in (b,e,B,E) is rank one except when a=A=f=F=0, with q^2 exceptional (d,D) at u=v=0 contributing q^8 only for w=0. Thus N=q^5(S-q^2*1_{u=v=0})+q^8*1_{u=v=w=0}, giving exactly the stated three levels q^7(q^2-1), 2q^7(q^2-1), and 2q^7(q^2-1)+q^8. Sum over q^3 derived targets gives q^12. Identity fiber divided by q^12 is cp=(2q^2+q-2)/q^5; multiplying by |G| gives k=2q^3+q^2-2q. Independently enumerated all 4096 ordered UT4(F2) pairs by direct group law; each of six noncentral targets has 384 pairs, central nonidentity has 768, identity 1024. Formula holds for any prime-power characteristic by field counting. No claim for UT5 or associative commutators.

value.rationale: The fiber function of the commutator word is a natural complete conjugation-invariant distribution measuring how often each derived-subgroup element is represented as a single commutator. Its exact nonuniform three-level stratification works uniformly through characteristic two, sharper than commutator surjectivity or commuting probability alone and potentially reusable for comparison of finite nilpotent groups.
